<div class="nv-rule" id="truthy-positions">

## Six syntax positions test truthiness; every other `bool` position stays checked

<div class="nv-rule-tags">
<span class="nv-rule-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span>
<span class="nv-rule-flag">Differs from PHP</span>
<a class="nv-rule-id" href="#truthy-positions"><code>expressions/truthy-positions</code></a>
</div>

Exactly six syntax positions test a value's truthiness instead of requiring it to already be `bool`:
`if`/`elseif`'s condition, `while`/`do…while`'s condition, `for`'s middle clause, the ternary and
elvis condition, and the operands of `&&`, `||` and `!`. Each accepts a value of **any** type —
`mixed`, a union, a scalar, an array, an object, an enum case, `callable` — with no diagnostic for
not already being `bool`, and answers by [`expressions/truthy-table`](/docs/rules/expressions/truthiness-and-equality/#truthy-table "The truthy table is PHP's, and bytes is falsy only when it is empty").

The list is closed and nothing narrower gets the exception. Assigning into a `bool`-typed parameter,
property, return or local still needs an explicit `as bool` or a comparison; `==` and `match` still
compare rather than test ([`expressions/switch-match-equality`](/docs/rules/expressions/truthiness-and-equality/#switch-match-equality "A switch label and a match arm compare by the equality rule and by nothing else")); `??` and `?->` test null against
not-null, which is a different axis and untouched.

A truthiness test converts nothing. It produces no value of a different type that can be read back,
assigned or passed on — it answers "branch or don't", freshly, every time — so a declared type never
changes here.

<aside class="nv-rule-diverges">
<p class="nv-rule-diverges-label">Where this differs from PHP</p>
<p>The implicit conversion to <code>bool</code> is confined to six positions, where PHP applies it wherever a <code>bool</code> is wanted</p>
</aside>

</div>

<div class="nv-rule" id="truthy-table">

## The truthy table is PHP's, and `bytes` is falsy only when it is empty

<div class="nv-rule-tags">
<span class="nv-rule-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span>
<span class="nv-rule-flag">Differs from PHP</span>
<a class="nv-rule-id" href="#truthy-table"><code>expressions/truthy-table</code></a>
</div>

A condition resolves PHP's own truthy table, over Novis's type set:

| type | falsy | truthy |
|---|---|---|
| `null` | always | never |
| `bool` | `false` | `true` |
| `int` / `uint` | `0` | anything else |
| `float` | `0.0`, including `-0.0`; `NAN` is truthy | anything else |
| `string` | `""` and the one-character `"0"` | every other string, `"0.0"` and `"false"` included |
| `bytes` | empty, and **only** empty | every non-empty buffer, the one-octet `"0"` included |
| `array<T>` | empty, for any `T` | one or more elements, whatever they hold |
| class instance, `callable` | never | always |
| enum case | never | always ([`enums/truthiness`](/docs/rules/enums/#truthiness "An enum case is always truthy, whatever integer backs it")) |
| `mixed`, a union | dispatched on the runtime tag, one row per tag | — |

**The `bytes` row is the one PHP does not supply, and it drops the `"0"` case deliberately.** That
exception exists because PHP reads a string as a possible number, and `bytes` is the type that never
converts to one. A `bytes` reaching a condition through a `mixed` takes the same row, so the two
spellings of one buffer never disagree.

Where the static type is a scalar, array, class, `callable` or enum, the compiler knows the row and
lowers to the matching native test with no dispatch. Only a `mixed` or union condition pays for a
runtime helper.

<aside class="nv-rule-diverges">
<p class="nv-rule-diverges-label">Where this differs from PHP</p>
<p><code>bytes</code> has no PHP neighbour and takes emptiness alone, so a one-octet <code>&quot;0&quot;</code> buffer is truthy where the string <code>&quot;0&quot;</code> is falsy</p>
</aside>

<dl class="nv-rule-meta"><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>See also</dt><dd><a href="/docs/rules/expressions/truthiness-and-equality/#truthy-positions" title="Six syntax positions test truthiness; every other bool position stays checked"><code>expressions/truthy-positions</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/enums/#truthiness" title="An enum case is always truthy, whatever integer backs it"><code>enums/truthiness</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/expressions/truthiness-and-equality/#equality-semantics" title="Equality has one row per type, and every row is the strict reading"><code>expressions/equality-semantics</code></a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Decided in</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0035.md">record 0035</a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0009.md">record 0009</a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0007.md">record 0007</a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Guarded by</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/tests/conformance/lang/a-bytes-in-a-condition-is-falsy-only-when-empty.nvst"><code>tests/conformance/lang/a-bytes-in-a-condition-is-falsy-only-when-empty.nvst</code></a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/tests/conformance/lang/a-mixed-in-a-condition-resolves-the-truthy-table-at-run-time.nvst"><code>tests/conformance/lang/a-mixed-in-a-condition-resolves-the-truthy-table-at-run-time.nvst</code></a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/tests/conformance/lang/empty-answers-the-truthy-table-for-every-nvs-type.nvst"><code>tests/conformance/lang/empty-answers-the-truthy-table-for-every-nvs-type.nvst</code></a></dd></div></dl>

</div>

<div class="nv-rule" id="no-keyword-logical-operators">

## `and`, `or` and `xor` do not parse, and `&&`/`||` are the whole set

<div class="nv-rule-tags">
<span class="nv-rule-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span>
<span class="nv-rule-flag">Differs from PHP</span>
<a class="nv-rule-id" href="#no-keyword-logical-operators"><code>expressions/no-keyword-logical-operators</code></a>
</div>

`and`, `or` and `xor` are rejected at parse time, in every position, as `E0226`. Each keyword is
still recognised where an infix logical operator would go, so the diagnostic can name the fix, but
the expression becomes an error node: there is no low-precedence AND or OR in the tree at all.

`&&` and `||` are the only logical connectives, at every precedence, and `!` is untouched. The
diagnostic for `and` and `or` names the one-token replacement.

`xor` has none. There is no `^^` operator, so its diagnostic names the two rewrites instead —
`(a || b) && !(a && b)` for the general truthy case, or `a != b` when both operands are already
`bool`. That is a real, narrow capability subtraction rather than a spelling change.

All three keywords stay reserved words. They are not freed for use as identifiers, which is what lets
the diagnostic fire at all.

<aside class="nv-rule-diverges">
<p class="nv-rule-diverges-label">Where this differs from PHP</p>
<p>The low-precedence keyword connectives are gone entirely, and <code>xor</code> has no operator replacement at all</p>
</aside>

<dl class="nv-rule-meta"><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>See also</dt><dd><a href="/docs/rules/expressions/truthiness-and-equality/#truthy-positions" title="Six syntax positions test truthiness; every other bool position stays checked"><code>expressions/truthy-positions</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/expressions/truthiness-and-equality/#one-equality-operator" title="== and != are the whole of equality, and ===, !== and &lt;&gt; do not parse"><code>expressions/one-equality-operator</code></a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Decided in</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0045.md">record 0045</a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0035.md">record 0035</a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0021.md">record 0021</a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Guarded by</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/tests/conformance/reject/keyword-logical-operators-do-not-parse.nvst"><code>tests/conformance/reject/keyword-logical-operators-do-not-parse.nvst</code></a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/tests/conformance/reject/xor-does-not-parse.nvst"><code>tests/conformance/reject/xor-does-not-parse.nvst</code></a></dd></div></dl>

</div>

<div class="nv-rule" id="nullable-condition-lint">

## A `?T` used directly as a condition is warned about, not refused

<div class="nv-rule-tags">
<span class="nv-rule-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span>
<a class="nv-rule-id" href="#nullable-condition-lint"><code>expressions/nullable-condition-lint</code></a>
</div>

`nvs check` warns when a `?T` is used directly as a condition, naming `!= null` as the fix.

Both `null` and `0` are falsy, so `if ($s as ?int)` is false for an invalid value *and* for a valid
zero — reconstructing precisely the `(int)$x > 0` defect that nullable conversion exists to remove.

It is a warning and not a diagnostic because **the hazard is not new and not specific to the
operator**: any `?int` in an `if` has always had it. Refusing it would narrow
[`expressions/truthy-positions`](/docs/rules/expressions/truthiness-and-equality/#truthy-positions "Six syntax positions test truthiness; every other bool position stays checked") for every nullable value in the language, which is a larger change
than this one.

No warning code is allocated yet, and `nvs check` does not emit this today.

<dl class="nv-rule-meta"><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>See also</dt><dd><a href="/docs/rules/expressions/conversion-and-intrinsics/#nullable-conversion" title="expr as ?T yields the converted value or null, and never throws"><code>expressions/nullable-conversion</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/expressions/truthiness-and-equality/#truthy-table" title="The truthy table is PHP's, and bytes is falsy only when it is empty"><code>expressions/truthy-table</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/expressions/pipeline-and-catch/#bare-throwable-arm-warns" title="An unbound catch (Throwable) arm that supplies a value is warned about"><code>expressions/bare-throwable-arm-warns</code></a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Decided in</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0066.md">record 0066</a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0035.md">record 0035</a></dd></div></dl>

</div>

<div class="nv-rule" id="one-equality-operator">

## `==` and `!=` are the whole of equality, and `===`, `!==` and `<>` do not parse

<div class="nv-rule-tags">
<span class="nv-rule-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span>
<span class="nv-rule-flag">Differs from PHP</span>
<a class="nv-rule-id" href="#one-equality-operator"><code>expressions/one-equality-operator</code></a>
</div>

There is **one** equality operator, `==`, and its negation `!=`. `===` and `!==` do not parse
(`E0232`); PHP's `<>` does not parse either (`E0241`), and each diagnostic names the edit. There is no
suppression and no dialect flag: a construct that parses in one project and not another is two
languages.

`!=` is exactly `!( … == … )`. There is no third relation.

Nothing for a second spelling to distinguish survives, because there is no loose comparison to escape
from. `==` never converts either operand; both operands must be able to hold the same value
([`expressions/disjoint-comparison-refused`](/docs/rules/expressions/truthiness-and-equality/#disjoint-comparison-refused "Comparing two types that no single value inhabits is a compile error")); each type's answer is the strict one
([`expressions/equality-semantics`](/docs/rules/expressions/truthiness-and-equality/#equality-semantics "Equality has one row per type, and every row is the strict reading")), objects compare by identity
([`expressions/object-identity-equality`](/docs/rules/expressions/truthiness-and-equality/#object-identity-equality "Two objects are equal only when they are the same object, and no class may change that")), and only a `mixed` or union pairing is decided at run
time ([`expressions/mixed-equality`](/docs/rules/expressions/truthiness-and-equality/#mixed-equality "A mixed or union operand resolves at run time, and a mismatched pair answers false")).

Ordering — `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=`, `<=>` — is a separate question with its own rule, and this operator
says nothing about it.

<aside class="nv-rule-diverges">
<p class="nv-rule-diverges-label">Where this differs from PHP</p>
<p>There is no loose-versus-strict pair to pick between — one operator, which never converts either operand</p>
</aside>

<div class="nv-rule" id="equality-semantics">

## Equality has one row per type, and every row is the strict reading

<div class="nv-rule-tags">
<span class="nv-rule-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span>
<span class="nv-rule-flag">Differs from PHP</span>
<a class="nv-rule-id" href="#equality-semantics"><code>expressions/equality-semantics</code></a>
</div>

Nothing converts. Each type has one row, and where PHP's two operators disagreed the row takes the
strict reading:

| type | two values are equal when |
|---|---|
| `null` | always — one value |
| `bool` | they are the same |
| `int`, `uint`, `float`, `decimal` | mathematically equal across the whole domain: `1 == 1.0` is true, and `decimal` ignores scale, so `1.10 == 1.1000` is true |
| `float` edges | IEEE 754: `NAN == NAN` is **false**, `0.0 == -0.0` is **true** |
| `string` | the same sequence of Unicode scalar values — never numeric, so `"1" == "01"` and `"1e3" == "1000"` are both false, and there is no normalization |
| `bytes` | the same bytes |
| `array<T>` | the same length, the same keys in the same order, and every value equal by this table, recursively |
| class instance | the same object ([`expressions/object-identity-equality`](/docs/rules/expressions/truthiness-and-equality/#object-identity-equality "Two objects are equal only when they are the same object, and no class may change that")) |
| enum case | the underlying integers are equal |
| `callable` | the same closure — two `fn` literals with identical bodies are two closures |
| `mixed`, a union | resolved at run time ([`expressions/mixed-equality`](/docs/rules/expressions/truthiness-and-equality/#mixed-equality "A mixed or union operand resolves at run time, and a mismatched pair answers false")) |

The array recursion terminates: an array is a copy-on-write value rather than a reference, so it
cannot contain itself. An array holding objects compares those by identity, which bounds that walk
too.

The natural ordering used for sorting is a separate question and answers differently for `float`; the
two are not the same table.

<aside class="nv-rule-diverges">
<p class="nv-rule-diverges-label">Where this differs from PHP</p>
<p>Each row where PHP's two operators disagreed takes <code>===</code>'s answer — two strings compare as text and never as numbers, and an array compares in key order</p>
</aside>

href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/tests/conformance/lang/equality-over-arrays-objects-and-mixed.nvst"><code>tests/conformance/lang/equality-over-arrays-objects-and-mixed.nvst</code></a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/tests/conformance/lang/float-comparisons-and-equality.nvst"><code>tests/conformance/lang/float-comparisons-and-equality.nvst</code></a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/tests/conformance/lang/two-nulls-are-equal-and-two-bools-order.nvst"><code>tests/conformance/lang/two-nulls-are-equal-and-two-bools-order.nvst</code></a></dd></div></dl>

</div>

<div class="nv-rule" id="mixed-equality">

## A `mixed` or union operand resolves at run time, and a mismatched pair answers `false`

<div class="nv-rule-tags">
<span class="nv-rule-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span>
<span class="nv-rule-flag">Differs from PHP</span>
<a class="nv-rule-id" href="#mixed-equality"><code>expressions/mixed-equality</code></a>
</div>

`$a == $b` where either side is `mixed` or a union compiles, dispatches on the runtime tags, and
applies [`expressions/equality-semantics`](/docs/rules/expressions/truthiness-and-equality/#equality-semantics "Equality has one row per type, and every row is the strict reading")'s table to the row they land in.

**When the two runtime tags belong to different rows, the answer is `false`.** It does not throw, and
it does not convert.

That is the strict answer, not a looser rule returning: a `string` and an `int` are not the same
value. The static case is a compile error rather than `false` for a different reason — there the
compiler can prove the answer before the program runs, which makes it dead code rather than a
question ([`expressions/disjoint-comparison-refused`](/docs/rules/expressions/truthiness-and-equality/#disjoint-comparison-refused "Comparing two types that no single value inhabits is a compile error")).

The asymmetry is worth stating plainly: **`mixed` is where you pay for not declaring a type.** A
comparison against `mixed` silently answers `false` where a typed one would have refused to compile.

<aside class="nv-rule-diverges">
<p class="nv-rule-diverges-label">Where this differs from PHP</p>
<p>A cross-type pairing is <code>false</code> rather than PHP's converting comparison, and it is the one place a comparison answers instead of refusing to compile</p>
</aside>

<dl class="nv-rule-meta"><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>See also</dt><dd><a href="/docs/rules/expressions/truthiness-and-equality/#disjoint-comparison-refused" title="Comparing two types that no single value inhabits is a compile error"><code>expressions/disjoint-comparison-refused</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/expressions/truthiness-and-equality/#equality-semantics" title="Equality has one row per type, and every row is the strict reading"><code>expressions/equality-semantics</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/expressions/truthiness-and-equality/#truthy-table" title="The truthy table is PHP's, and bytes is falsy only when it is empty"><code>expressions/truthy-table</code></a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Decided in</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0090.md">record 0090</a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0007.md">record 0007</a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Guarded by</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/tests/conformance/lang/numeric-identity-is-one-domain-at-runtime.nvst"><code>tests/conformance/lang/numeric-identity-is-one-domain-at-runtime.nvst</code></a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/tests/conformance/lang/equality-over-arrays-objects-and-mixed.nvst"><code>tests/conformance/lang/equality-over-arrays-objects-and-mixed.nvst</code></a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/crates/nvs-types/tests/equality.rs"><code>crates/nvs-types/tests/equality.rs</code></a></dd></div></dl>

</div>

<div class="nv-rule" id="object-identity-equality">

## Two objects are equal only when they are the same object, and no class may change that

<div class="nv-rule-tags">
<span class="nv-rule-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span>
<span class="nv-rule-flag">Differs from PHP</span>
<a class="nv-rule-id" href="#object-identity-equality"><code>expressions/object-identity-equality</code></a>
</div>

`$a == $b` on two class instances asks whether they are the same object. It never walks properties.

There is **no `__equals`, no `equals()` protocol and no `Equatable` interface**. A per-class equality
hook would make `==` mean something different in every file, and an ambient, undeclared property walk
has unbounded cost in the object graph's size with no way for a class to opt out.

Two named ways to ask the other question already exist:

- **`$a->compareTo($b) == 0`**, where the class implements `Comparable`. A class with a meaningful
  notion of "same value" almost always has a meaningful order too, and this gets both from one
  declaration.
- **`Core\Test::assertEqualsDeep`** in a test, which walks properties, arrays and shapes and produces
  a diff. It is a test member on purpose: a structural walk is a debugging affordance, not something a
  request path should reach for by accident.

A class needing content equality in production and wanting no order writes an ordinary named method.
That reads worse than `==` by exactly one call, and it is visible at the call site.

<aside class="nv-rule-diverges">
<p class="nv-rule-diverges-label">Where this differs from PHP</p>
<p>PHP's <code>==</code> walked properties; here there is no property walk, no <code>__equals</code>, no <code>equals()</code> protocol and no <code>Equatable</code> interface</p>
</aside>

<dl class="nv-rule-meta"><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>See also</dt><dd><a href="/docs/rules/expressions/truthiness-and-equality/#equality-semantics" title="Equality has one row per type, and every row is the strict reading"><code>expressions/equality-semantics</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/expressions/truthiness-and-equality/#one-equality-operator" title="== and != are the whole of equality, and ===, !== and &lt;&gt; do not parse"><code>expressions/one-equality-operator</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/expressions/truthiness-and-equality/#mixed-equality" title="A mixed or union operand resolves at run time, and a mismatched pair answers false"><code>expressions/mixed-equality</code></a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Decided in</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0090.md">record 0090</a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0013.md">record 0013</a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0014.md">record 0014</a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0028.md">record 0028</a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0079.md">record 0079</a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Guarded by</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/tests/conformance/lang/equality-over-arrays-objects-and-mixed.nvst"><code>tests/conformance/lang/equality-over-arrays-objects-and-mixed.nvst</code></a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/tests/conformance/core/object-collections-hold-one-member-per-distinct-value.nvst"><code>tests/conformance/core/object-collections-hold-one-member-per-distinct-value.nvst</code></a></dd></div></dl>

</div>

<div class="nv-rule" id="disjoint-comparison-refused">

## Comparing two types that no single value inhabits is a compile error

<div class="nv-rule-tags">
<span class="nv-rule-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span>
<span class="nv-rule-flag">Differs from PHP</span>
<a class="nv-rule-id" href="#disjoint-comparison-refused"><code>expressions/disjoint-comparison-refused</code></a>
</div>

A comparison whose two static types are **disjoint** — no single value inhabits both — is a compile
error (`E0466`), because the compiler already knows the answer and the author did not mean to write
it.

```
string $s = "1";
int $n = 1;
if ($s == $n) { }               // E0466: `string` and `int` are disjoint
if ($s == ($n as string)) { }   // convert once, deliberately, then compare
```

Disjointness, not identity of types, is the test, so ordinary code still compiles: the same type; any
pairing of `int`, `uint`, `float` and `decimal`, which are **one numeric domain**; `?T` against `null`
or against `T`, which is the null test and narrows; a union against any type one member can hold; a
literal or enum-case type against its base; `mixed` against anything; a class against itself or an
ancestor.

Refused: a non-nullable type against `null`; `string` against `bytes`; an enum against its underlying
integer, where `$e as int` is the written spelling; two unrelated classes; and anything else disjoint.

This turns the entire class of comparisons that silently answered `false` — or answered `true` in PHP
7 and `false` in PHP 8 — into a diagnostic at the site that wrote it.

<aside class="nv-rule-diverges">
<p class="nv-rule-diverges-label">Where this differs from PHP</p>
<p><code>&quot;1&quot; == 1</code> neither answers <code>true</code> nor <code>false</code>; it does not compile, and the diagnostic names the conversion the author meant</p>
</aside>

<dl class="nv-rule-meta"><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>See also</dt><dd><a href="/docs/rules/expressions/truthiness-and-equality/#one-equality-operator" title="== and != are the whole of equality, and ===, !== and &lt;&gt; do not parse"><code>expressions/one-equality-operator</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/expressions/truthiness-and-equality/#equality-semantics" title="Equality has one row per type, and every row is the strict reading"><code>expressions/equality-semantics</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/expressions/truthiness-and-equality/#mixed-equality" title="A mixed or union operand resolves at run time, and a mismatched pair answers false"><code>expressions/mixed-equality</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/expressions/truthiness-and-equality/#switch-match-equality" title="A switch label and a match arm compare by the equality rule and by nothing else"><code>expressions/switch-match-equality</code></a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Decided in</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0090.md">record 0090</a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0007.md">record 0007</a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0009.md">record 0009</a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0010.md">record 0010</a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0047.md">record 0047</a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0054.md">record 0054</a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Guarded by</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/tests/conformance/lang/disjoint-equality-is-a-compile-error.nvst"><code>tests/conformance/lang/disjoint-equality-is-a-compile-error.nvst</code></a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/tests/conformance/lang/equality-across-overlapping-types-still-compiles.nvst"><code>tests/conformance/lang/equality-across-overlapping-types-still-compiles.nvst</code></a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/crates/nvs-types/tests/equality.rs"><code>crates/nvs-types/tests/equality.rs</code></a></dd></div></dl>

</div>

<div class="nv-rule" id="switch-match-equality">

## A `switch` label and a `match` arm compare by the equality rule and by nothing else

<div class="nv-rule-tags">
<span class="nv-rule-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span>
<span class="nv-rule-flag">Differs from PHP</span>
<a class="nv-rule-id" href="#switch-match-equality"><code>expressions/switch-match-equality</code></a>
</div>

A `switch` label and a `match` arm are compared against the subject by
[`expressions/equality-semantics`](/docs/rules/expressions/truthiness-and-equality/#equality-semantics "Equality has one row per type, and every row is the strict reading"), and by nothing else. There is one comparison in the language,
so there is one here.

A label or arm whose static type is disjoint from the subject's is
[`expressions/disjoint-comparison-refused`](/docs/rules/expressions/truthiness-and-equality/#disjoint-comparison-refused "Comparing two types that no single value inhabits is a compile error")'s compile error, at the label rather than at the
`switch`.

`match (true) { … }` is unaffected: each arm is a `bool`, tested against `true`.

Truthiness has no part in this. A `switch` subject and a `match` subject are compared, never tested
for truth, and [`expressions/truthy-positions`](/docs/rules/expressions/truthiness-and-equality/#truthy-positions "Six syntax positions test truthiness; every other bool position stays checked")'s six positions do not include either.

<aside class="nv-rule-diverges">
<p class="nv-rule-diverges-label">Where this differs from PHP</p>
<p><code>switch</code> no longer compares loosely while <code>match</code> compares identically — there is one comparison, and both use it</p>
</aside>

<dl class="nv-rule-meta"><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>See also</dt><dd><a href="/docs/rules/expressions/truthiness-and-equality/#one-equality-operator" title="== and != are the whole of equality, and ===, !== and &lt;&gt; do not parse"><code>expressions/one-equality-operator</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/expressions/truthiness-and-equality/#disjoint-comparison-refused" title="Comparing two types that no single value inhabits is a compile error"><code>expressions/disjoint-comparison-refused</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/expressions/truthiness-and-equality/#equality-semantics" title="Equality has one row per type, and every row is the strict reading"><code>expressions/equality-semantics</code></a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Decided in</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0090.md">record 0090</a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0035.md">record 0035</a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Guarded by</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/tests/conformance/lang/a-switch-compares-in-order-and-falls-through.nvst"><code>tests/conformance/lang/a-switch-compares-in-order-and-falls-through.nvst</code></a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/tests/conformance/lang/equality-across-overlapping-types-still-compiles.nvst"><code>tests/conformance/lang/equality-across-overlapping-types-still-compiles.nvst</code></a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/tests/differential/lang/a-switch-and-a-match-agree-with-php.nvst"><code>tests/differential/lang/a-switch-and-a-match-agree-with-php.nvst</code></a></dd></div></dl>

</div>
